parts.gloss: pronominal suffix for those who do
that which they are skilled in (with metrical elongation and 'even' suffix)

words.gloss: even that which they are skilled in

literal: Those who do not know the assembly, those who undertake speaking, do not know the types of speech, and even that which they are skilled in does not exist.
translation: Those who undertake to speak without understanding the nature of their audience do not comprehend the power of words; even the knowledge they are skilled in becomes utterly worthless.
modern: அவையின் தன்மையை அறியாமல் பேசுதலைத் தொடங்குபவர்கள், சொற்களின் வகைகளை அறியாதவர்கள் ஆவர்; அவர்கள் கற்றறிந்த கல்வியும் பயனில்லாததாகிவிடும்.
explanation: This couplet emphasizes the importance of understanding one's audience before speaking. Those who rush to speak without assessing the nature, intellect, and mood of the assembly (அவை) demonstrate a lack of understanding of the power and classification of words (சொல்லின் வகை). Even if they possess deep knowledge or skill (வல்லதூஉம்) in a particular subject, it becomes completely useless and non-existent (இல்) because it is delivered in an inappropriate forum. True eloquence requires not just subject knowledge, but also the wisdom to adapt it to the audience.
